plan.question: Do the podocytes this atlas calls 'endocytic' really carry LRP2 and CUBN, or is that segmentation?
plan.summary: Two audit_population steps test LRP2 and CUBN separately in NPHS1-anchored podocytes (label rule nphs1-anchored-v1, which ignores LRP2/CUBN for podocyte membership, avoiding circular labelling) across all 21 distinct sections (duplicate GSM8720419 excluded) under default versus nucleus-only and distance-capped assignment. Nothing testable in the question is left out; controls are decided by the agent after each audit per instructions.

steps.rationale: Testing LRP2 in podocytes defined independently of LRP2/CUBN under progressively stricter molecule assignment checks whether its signal survives removal of likely segmentation admixture.

Testing CUBN separately in podocytes defined independently of LRP2/CUBN under the same stricter assignment conditions checks whether the second endocytic marker also survives removal of likely segmentation admixture.

sub_claims.text: Podocytes labelled independently of endocytic genes carry LRP2 only because of segmentation/admixture, so LRP2 expression should drop under stricter assignment.
Podocytes labelled independently of endocytic genes carry CUBN only because of segmentation/admixture, so CUBN expression should drop under stricter assignment.

verdict.question: Do the podocytes this atlas calls 'endocytic' really carry LRP2 and CUBN, or is that segmentation?
verdict.scope: In these sections and regions, under the controls each claim cites. A verdict says what this evidence supports, not whether the biology is true.

sub_claim.text: Podocytes labelled independently of endocytic genes carry LRP2 only because of segmentation/admixture, so LRP2 expression should drop under stricter assignment.
Podocytes labelled independently of endocytic genes carry CUBN only because of segmentation/admixture, so CUBN expression should drop under stricter assignment.

verdict.rule: A sub-claim rests on the non-injected claims about its cell type and any of its genes. Each verified claim's outcome is 'holds' when its evidence label is stable and 'drops' when it is segmentation-sensitive. Confirmed: every claim is verified with an outcome, and every outcome is the predicted one. Refuted: every claim is verified with an outcome, and every outcome is the opposite. Inconclusive: no claim, a claim that is not verified (failed, disputed, unavailable or pending), insufficient evidence, or outcomes that disagree.
